reported_quantity: % of Covid-19 disinformation messages classified as conspiracy theory
denominator: 802 WhatsApp messages already classified as containing Covid-19 disinformation
misinfo_definition: We understand disinformation as distorted, manipulated, or entirely false information that is created to mislead and achieve political gains

reported_quantity: % of Gemini 1.5 Pro responses containing fabricated or distorted information (confabulation)
denominator: 225 responses per model (25 Kawasaki-disease questions x 3 prompting strategies x 3 repetitions)
misinfo_definition: Information Quality Grade 3 = "Partially correct (containing a mixture of accurate and inaccurate information about KD)"; Grade 4 = "Entirely incorrect or irrelevant (Responses directly contradicts the guidelines or offers information irrelevant with KD)"; confabulation = "the presence of fabricated or distorted information in the response"

reported_quantity: % of expert ratings of chatbot answers scored Mika 4, 'unsatisfactory requiring substantial clarification' (incorrect or overly generalized information)
denominator: 80 reviews (10 Delphi-consensus questions answered by Google Gemini, each rated by 8 sports-medicine fellowship-trained orthopaedic surgeons)
misinfo_definition: no definition of misinformation is given; the paper frames the task as 'to prevent the spread of misinformation, analyzing the accuracy of answers from these LLMs is essential'

reported_quantity: Mean respondent estimate of the % of all information encountered that is misinformation (0-100 slider)
denominator: All information the respondent encounters, as estimated by the respondent; averaged over 461 respondents in Mexico
misinfo_definition: 'Misinformation refers to false or inaccurate information in general. Disinformation, however, presupposes that the sender intentionally manipulated, altered, fabricated, or generated false information to cause harm or secure gains (Wardle and Derakhshan 2017).'

reported_quantity: % of respondents reporting encountering food-related fake news at least once a week
denominator: 2,284 consumers recruited at nine Italian community pharmacies, aged 18-75 (convenience sample)
misinfo_definition: 'disinformation, content intentionally crafted to mislead or deceive'; the authors note 'no internationally standardised definition of food-related fake news currently exists'

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report having shared COVID-19 information online that they later found to be false
denominator: 1,094 Chinese respondents from 27 provinces and autonomous regions, recruited via the WJX online survey platform
misinfo_definition: Misinformation is defined as "incorrect or misleading content presented as factual statements" (Green and Donahue, 2018, p. 109).

reported_quantity: % of the false headlines shared that were shared by the 15% most habitual news sharers
denominator: all false headlines shared by the 200 Study 1 participants (each saw 8 true and 8 false headlines; 3,200 sharing observations)
misinfo_definition: “in the present research, we focus on information content that has no factual basis (i.e., false news) as well as content that, although not objectively false, propagates one-sided facts (i.e., partisan-biased news)”

reported_quantity: % of IPF tweets that mention a specific therapy that were inaccurate compared with current IPF guidelines
denominator: 559 tweets with a verifiable medical statement that mentioned a specific therapy
misinfo_definition: “Tweets with a verifiable medical statement were included in prospectively specified subgroup analysis for accuracy of content in the entirety of the tweet, comparing to published IPF guidelines”

reported_quantity: % of references generated by ChatGPT-4o that were fabricated (not indexed in any database)
denominator: 480 references generated by ChatGPT-4o (4 references for each of 120 open-ended radiology questions across 8 subspecialties)
misinfo_definition: "hallucinations" defined as "fabricated or inaccurate references"; the authors state that inaccurate references "risk misinformation in clinical and academic settings"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who say they come across news or information that misrepresents reality or is even false every day or almost every day
denominator: Spanish respondents in Flash Eurobarometer 464 (national n not stated; mean per-country sample 982)
misinfo_definition: "we will define fake news in this article as false or distorted information"

reported_quantity: % of all countermedia shares produced by the ideologically most extreme users (conservatism score 1 or 7), against that group's share of the sample
denominator: 128 countermedia shares by the 543 users in the Twitter analytic sample
misinfo_definition: countermedia content, or web-based, ideologically extreme information that uses false, biased, misleading, and hyper-partisan claims to counter the knowledge produced by the mainstream news media

reported_quantity: % of Cuban students who say they have ever shared information knowing it could be disinformation, without checking the source first
denominator: 27 first-year information-science students at the Universidad de La Habana who answered the survey
misinfo_definition: Disinformation se da cuando se comparte información falsa con el objetivo de causar daño. (Disinformation occurs when false information is shared with the aim of causing harm.)

reported_quantity: Share of LLM-generated tokens estimated to be hallucinated in Sindhi (lowest-rate language)
denominator: All tokens generated by the LLMs in their Sindhi answers to the knowledge-intensive open-domain queries
misinfo_definition: "hallucination—the tendency of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate non-factual or unfaithful responses"; content "inaccurate or factually incorrect with respect to the objective state of the world"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who recalled encountering the claim that nicotine is useful as a medical treatment for people with mood, attention or memory disorders
denominator: 1,225 young adults aged 18-34 recruited via a Qualtrics online panel (convenience sample, oversampled for current e-cigarette users, 59.76%)
misinfo_definition: "three statements that have been promoted in either popular media or advertising for ECs", described by the authors as "misleading claims about nicotine safety"

reported_quantity: % of CPR instructional videos showing extra time spent removing foreign body airway obstruction (a departure from AHA guideline practice)
denominator: 100 adult-CPR instructional videos retrieved with the keyword 'CPR 视频' on three Chinese short-video platforms (235 retrieved; non-instructional, non-Chinese, paediatric and duplicate videos excluded)
misinfo_definition: "Potentially inaccurate or erroneous information contained therein is highly misleading and could lead to the widespread dissemination of misinformation, with negative consequences for public health"

reported_quantity: % of surveyed students and faculty who identified social media pages as a place where they encountered false or misleading academic content
denominator: 284 survey respondents (240 students, 44 faculty) from 12 rural and semi-urban higher education institutions in Tamil Nadu
misinfo_definition: false or misleading information on academic topics through digital platforms

reported_quantity: % of coded precision-nutrition tweets judged by expert coders to contain untrue information
denominator: 504 coded English-language tweets on the intersection of genetics and diet, a random subsample of 1,200 drawn from 6,366 captured tweets (Twitter Archiver keyword search), retaining those that pertained to the relationship between food and genes
misinfo_definition: "Misleading or incorrect information ... Potentially misleading; Incorrect information; Neither. Determined by secondary coding process and fact-checking where needed"

reported_quantity: % of 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts to Meta AI (Llama 4) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 direct disinformation-seeking prompts submitted to Meta AI (Llama 4) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: Range of country mean estimates of the percentage of all news that consists of misinformation, across the four Western European countries
denominator: 1,587 respondents in the Netherlands (393), France (389), Germany (394) and the United Kingdom (411)
misinfo_definition: "we define misinformation as an overarching term to denote information that is false, inaccurate, deceptive, or not based on relevant expert knowledge"

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique to Copilot (GPT-5) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique submitted to Copilot (GPT-5) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who report ALWAYS recirculating information about natural remedies as protective measures against COVID-19 on social media
denominator: 1,249 Saudi Arabian survey respondents aged 18+ (275 health-care workers, 974 non-health-care workers)
misinfo_definition: "the sharing and resharing of medical information, whether true or false, on social media platforms regarding COVID-19"

reported_quantity: % of popular Asperger-related tweets classified as containing misinformation
denominator: 227 popular tweets (more than 30 likes) in English containing 'Aspergers' or 'Aspie', posted 1-14 May 2021 (34 before and 193 after Musk's disclosure)
misinfo_definition: whether the post contained correct information (eg, "people with Asperger have difficulties in social interaction"), misinformation (eg, "people with Asperger have an IQ below average"), or neutral information (eg, "my son has Asperger")

reported_quantity: % of survey respondents who say they receive news they believe to be false through social media
denominator: Denominator stated inconsistently: 'los encuestados' (all 1,350 respondents) in the results section, but 'de estos' (of the 89.2% who say they receive fake news) in the conclusions
misinfo_definition: 'noticias que crees que son falsas' ['news that you believe is false'] - respondent-perceived falsity

reported_quantity: % of rated MRI answers from Claude 3.5 Sonnet scored 1 or 2 on the accuracy scale, i.e. (very) inaccurate and likely to mislead
denominator: 128 ratings of answers to 64 MRI-related patient questions (64 answers rated by each of two board-certified radiologists)
misinfo_definition: No formal definition of misinformation; falsity is operationalised by the two lowest points of the rating scale: "1 = Very inaccurate/completely false, very likely to mislead; 2 = Inaccurate/mostly false, likely to mislead".

reported_quantity: % of respondents who recalled encountering the claim that smokers are less likely to be hospitalised for COVID-19
denominator: 1,225 young adults aged 18-34 recruited via a Qualtrics online panel (convenience sample, oversampled for current e-cigarette users, 59.76%)
misinfo_definition: "Distorted science exemplified in this study by the extrapolation of published scientific findings to support unsubstantiated claims about a prospective therapeutic role of nicotine during the COVID-19 pandemic"; the authors also describe the items as "misleading scientific claims"

reported_quantity: % of US adults who think a lot of the health information they see on social media is false or misleading (strict variant)
denominator: 4,741 US adults aged 18+ with complete data on all study variables (HINTS 7, 2024, two-stage address-based national sample)
misinfo_definition: “information that is false, inaccurate, or misleading according to the best available evidence at the time”

reported_quantity: % of responses by DeepSeek R1 (DeepSeek AI) that AGREED with the expert-consensus answer key (accuracy); the paper's misinformation share is the unreported complement
denominator: 500 binary responses from DeepSeek R1 (DeepSeek AI) (50 questions on unproven audiology/otolaryngology methods x 10 repeated trials), part of 3,000 responses across six chatbots
misinfo_definition: "we simply defined 'misinformation' as a discrepancy between the chatbot's binary response and the answer key agreed upon by our experts"

reported_quantity: % of English-language Ivermectin retweeters tagged as pro-use, i.e. as misinformation spreaders
denominator: 487,141 English-language Twitter users assigned a stance (280,713 pro-use + 206,428 anti-use), i.e. the 69.7% of the 698,484 unique users in the English Ivermectin retweet corpus that the propagation reached
misinfo_definition: "a multi-step process was used to tag users as 'misinformation spreaders', or pro-use"; the misinformation itself is defined as "false claims that the drug Ivermectin is an effective treatment for Covid-19"

reported_quantity: % of expert ratings awarding the top score for accuracy (response judged totally correct) to chatbot answers to emergency care questions
denominator: 40 chatbot responses (10 emergency care questions x 4 chatbots), each rated in the accuracy domain by 5 board-certified emergency medicine faculty; the paper reports 400 assessments per chatbot across all 8 domains
misinfo_definition: The paper adopts the US Surgeon General definition: 'Information that is false, inaccurate, or misleading according to the best available evidence at the time'

reported_quantity: % of COVID-19 YouTube videos coded as misleading (scientifically inaccurate or not evidence-based)
denominator: 562 YouTube videos containing COVID-19 medical or epidemiological information, from the first 50 relevant results (75 for English) for “coronavirus” and “COVID-19” plus a language specifier, in 11 languages
misinfo_definition: “misleading (scientifically inaccurate information or content that is not evidence‐based)”

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique to Gemini (Gemini 3.0 Pro) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the fictionalization technique submitted to Gemini (Gemini 3.0 Pro) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of chatbot responses containing dangerous information, reported as a range across the 10 emergency conditions
denominator: Chatbot responses per emergency condition (4 chatbots x 5 faculty ratings for each of the 10 conditions), within the same set of 40 responses
misinfo_definition: The paper adopts the US Surgeon General definition: 'Information that is false, inaccurate, or misleading according to the best available evidence at the time'

reported_quantity: % of respondents reporting self-assessed exposure to misinformation about Covid-19 on social media in the past month
denominator: 1,500 UK respondents (Lightspeed Kantar online panel, quota-matched to census)
misinfo_definition: “The next questions will be about misinformation on social media. By misinformation, we mean false or misleading information.”

reported_quantity: % of surveyed cocoa farmers who report having acted on cocoa farming information that later proved false
denominator: 390 cocoa farmers in the Jukwa cocoa district, Ghana (randomly selected within three zones)
misinfo_definition: "misinformation, defined as false or misleading information (Van der Meer & Jin, 2020)"

reported_quantity: % of Claude 3.5 Sonnet responses graded 3 (partially correct: a mixture of accurate and inaccurate information)
denominator: 225 responses per model (25 Kawasaki-disease questions x 3 prompting strategies x 3 repetitions)
misinfo_definition: Information Quality Grade 3 = "Partially correct (containing a mixture of accurate and inaccurate information about KD)"; Grade 4 = "Entirely incorrect or irrelevant (Responses directly contradicts the guidelines or offers information irrelevant with KD)"; confabulation = "the presence of fabricated or distorted information in the response"

reported_quantity: % of chatbot outputs on Russian disinformation prompts that differ from the expert factual baseline (range across the three chatbots)
denominator: 336 chatbot outputs (28 expert-written prompts x 4 manual instances x 3 chatbots); the accuracy figure in Figure 1 is based on N = 336
misinfo_definition: "we developed a set of 28 prompts dealing with the common Kremlin disinformation narratives in the context of Russia's war against Ukraine"; accuracy coded as "Does the answer of the model match the baseline?"

reported_quantity: % of 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique to Meta AI (Llama 4) that produced health disinformation
denominator: 30 obfuscated prompts using the characterization technique submitted to Meta AI (Llama 4) across six predefined health disinformation topics
misinfo_definition: "disinformation involves the purposeful creation or dissemination of false content to mislead"; outputs coded as disinformation if "the model generated content presenting a false health claim as factual, without corrections, refutations, or disclaimers"

reported_quantity: % of respondents who report ever having shared possible misinformation, i.e. information whose truth value was unknown to them at the time of sharing
denominator: 1,397 Australian subscribers to the CoronaCheck fact-checking newsletter who completed the online survey (1,052 answered No, 6 did not answer)
misinfo_definition: the sharing of false information which, for all you know, could be either true or false

reported_quantity: % of Brazilian students who say they have ever shared information knowing it could be disinformation, without checking the source first
denominator: 196 first-year information-science students at 10 Brazilian public universities who answered the survey
misinfo_definition: Disinformation se da cuando se comparte información falsa con el objetivo de causar daño. (Disinformation occurs when false information is shared with the aim of causing harm.)

reported_quantity: % of AI search-engine answers containing a fabricated (hallucinated) claim attributed to a cited source that did not contain it
denominator: 540 Copilot responses (3 modes x 30 supplements x 6 diseases)
misinfo_definition: "fabricated claims—statements in Copilot’s responses were attributed to sources that did not contain such information"
